overview: Mainfreight is a New Zealand-founded, NZX-listed global supply-chain logistics group operating an integrated network of Domestic Transport, Warehousing, and Air & Ocean freight forwarding businesses across New Zealand, Australia, Asia, Europe and the Americas. Listed on the NZX since 1996, the group generated NZ$5.38 billion of revenue and NZ$350.9 million of profit before tax in FY2026 (year to 31 March 2026) from 331 branches in 27 countries and 10,839 team members. It is a self-styled '100-year vision' owner-operator business, deliberately decentralised into branch-level profit centres, and unusual among global forwarders in owning a large share of the property (warehouses/cross-docks) it operates from rather than leasing or asset-light brokering.

business_model.summary: Mainfreight earns freight and logistics revenue across three integrated divisions - Domestic Transport (road/rail), Warehousing, and Air & Ocean freight forwarding - and reports both gross Total Revenue and a post-direct-freight-cost 'gross margin'/return-on-revenue metric by division and region, reflecting that a large share of Transport Costs (freight, cartage, agent and carrier costs) are pass-through in nature. Growth strategy is to increase branch density and market share in mature regions (NZ, Australia) while building out immature networks (Europe, Americas, Asia) toward profitability, funded by internally generated cash and moderate leverage rather than M&A.

revenue_streams.name: Domestic Transport
revenue_streams.notes: FY2026 revenue NZ$2,492.9m, PBT $154.7m, 6.2% return-on-revenue (down from 7.5% FY2025)

revenue_streams.name: Air & Ocean Forwarding
revenue_streams.notes: FY2026 revenue NZ$1,980.8m (down from $2,108.2m), PBT $135.0m, 6.8% ROR; most exposed to freight-rate cycle

revenue_streams.name: Warehousing
revenue_streams.notes: FY2026 revenue NZ$909.8m, PBT $61.2m, 6.7% ROR; underpinned by owned/long-lease property (1.1m m2 globally)

business_model.customer_type: B2B; predominantly SME and mid-market importers/exporters in food, beverage, retail and general trade verticals, plus larger enterprise supply-chain customers (top 500 customers ~41% of revenue per FY2026 five-year roadmap); no single customer exceeds 10% of any segment's revenue
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2026 revenue by region: New Zealand $1.2b (~34% of PBT), Australia $1.7b (~44% of PBT), Europe $1.2b, Americas $1.0b, Asia $0.2b. 66% of Group revenue and the large majority of profit is generated offshore (non-NZ). Australia's profitability now exceeds New Zealand's for the first time (from FY2025), and NZ+Australia together generate the great majority of Group profit while Europe, Americas and Asia remain sub-scale or loss-making by comparison.

main_competitors: Toll Group / Team Global Express (Australia domestic)
regional owner-drivers and 3PLs in each market
competitive_position.market_position: A mid-sized global player relative to the DSV/Kuehne+Nagel/DHL top tier, but a market-share leader in its home markets of New Zealand and Australia (domestic transport and warehousing) and a credible, growing niche player in international Air & Ocean forwarding. Management explicitly targets long-term market-share gains through the cycle rather than scale via acquisition.

moat_factors.description: Deep, unusually long-tenured branch and country management (regional leaders with 15-31 years' tenure) with devolved P&L accountability; culture is repeatedly cited by management and independent analysts as the core differentiator and is difficult for scaled, centrally-managed competitors to replicate
331 branches in 27 countries combining road, rail, warehousing, air and ocean gives connected, consistent service between small towns and major hubs, particularly dominant in NZ/Australia

Over 1.1m m2 of warehousing and significant owned land/buildings (property carrying value ~NZ$1.53bn) versus mostly asset-light peers who lease; provides balance-sheet backing, control of service quality and a hedge against rising lease costs, but ties up capital and slows expansion pace in new regions
Explicit multi-decade planning horizon (five- and even six-year public roadmaps to 2031) supports patient capital allocation through freight cycles, unusual for a listed company
Directors and founder-related entities hold ~19.7% of shares, aligning incentives with long-term shareholders

weaknesses: Sub-scale outside NZ/Australia: Europe, Americas and Asia remain either marginally profitable or loss-making (Americas PBT was -$7.9m/-1.3% margin in FY2026) after many years of investment, versus scaled global peers already profitable in those geographies
Asset-medium/capital-intensive model requires continuous heavy capex (~$174-234m guided for FY2027) which depresses free cash flow and ROIC versus asset-light forwarders
Limited pricing power in Air & Ocean relative to scale leaders (DSV/Kuehne+Nagel/DHL) who have greater carrier buying power
Decentralised model can slow response to a rapidly declining freight-rate/demand environment, as evidenced by the FY2026 H1 cost/efficiency lag

growth_drivers: Continued NZ/Australia network intensification and market-share capture, where profitability and returns remain highest
European network build-out (targeting circa 80 branches long-term) contingent on profitability improvement; currently ~10 countries with ~80% of European profit from Netherlands/Belgium
Americas expansion (New York, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles; new Toronto warehouse) - the region with 'the greatest amount of potential' per management but currently the weakest financial performer
Asia network growth (11 countries currently, targeting 35 branches across 15 countries by FY2029) as a long-term contributor to global trade flows
Warehousing capex programme: new larger-format, more automated cross-docks and warehouses (e.g., Brisbane, Christchurch, Willawong) improving efficiency and unit economics
Supply-chain/vertical-integration cross-sell (customs, refrigerated transport, rail, perishables, hazardous goods) deepening share of wallet with top-500 customers
Technology/AI adoption (in-house software platforms, robotics in warehouses, predictive analytics, generative AI in operations) targeted at efficiency gains
Long-stated aspirational target of $10 billion Group revenue by FY2029/30 per the five-year roadmap

business.description: Air & Ocean margins are highly sensitive to global sea/air freight rate swings; FY2026 saw Air & Ocean revenue fall ~6% and PBT margin compress, while ocean rates are forecast to fall sharply again in 2026 amid overcapacity and Red Sea route normalisation

Both regions have underperformed for years; Americas PBT went negative in FY2026 (-1.3% margin) and management explicitly says these networks 'require significant profit improvement' before further capital or lease commitments
Heavy exposure to food, beverage and retail trade verticals and reliance on global trade volumes generally

business.risk: Competitive intensity from larger scaled forwarders
business.description: DSV's 2025 acquisition of DB Schenker created a scale rival to Kuehne+Nagel; larger players have greater carrier buying power and may compress margins

financial.description: 66% of Group revenue generated offshore (AUD, USD, EUR); NZD movements materially affect reported results - FY2026 constant-currency revenue growth was actually -0.2% and PBT -10.7% versus reported +2.8%/-8.5%
IFRS16 lease liabilities of ~NZ$1.29bn and rising depreciation/finance costs on right-of-use assets; interest cover fell from 8.82x to 7.01x in FY2026
Labour expenses rose 8.7% in FY2026 versus 2.8% revenue growth, a key driver of margin compression; management explicitly flagged being 'slow to adjust internal cost structures' in H1 FY2026
Middle East conflict-driven diesel cost increases beginning to bite from late FY2026, though largely recoverable via fuel adjustment factors

regulatory.description: Group qualifies as an in-scope MNE; no material current impact expected for FY2026 but requires ongoing monitoring across multiple jurisdictions

regulatory.risk: Trade tariffs and customs policy shifts
regulatory.description: US tariff implementation (average ~18%, highest since 1930s) disrupted international supply chains and customer trade patterns during FY2026, though the group navigated this 'satisfactorily' per management

macro.description: Business is a direct proxy for global and domestic trade volumes; a global trade slowdown or recession would compress both Transport and Air & Ocean volumes simultaneously

Bank term loans and lease finance costs are largely floating rate (Group elected not to enter swaps); a 100bp rate move affects post-tax profit by ~$0.2m directly, but capex funding costs are a bigger indirect sensitivity

macro.risk: New Zealand/Australia demographic and cost-of-living pressures
macro.description: Chairman has flagged ageing-population/immigration policy risk to New Zealand's long-term labour supply and growth

execution.description: 83-year-old founder Bruce Plested remains Chairman with no announced succession plan; long-tenured board (Bryan Mogridge retiring after 23 years at the July 2026 AGM); heavy reliance on long-serving regional leaders and GMD Don Braid for the decentralised culture that underpins the moat

Mainfreight has historically traded at a premium P/E to global logistics peers reflecting its quality/growth reputation; any sustained earnings disappointment (as in FY2026) risks material multiple de-rating

execution.risk: Capital allocation discipline in loss-making regions
execution.description: Continued investment commitment to Europe/Americas despite years of underperformance carries execution and capital-efficiency risk if profitability inflection is delayed further

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global freight forwarding market estimated to grow from ~US$170bn (2026) to ~US$268bn by 2035 (~5.2% CAGR), but near-term 2026 outlook is soft: ocean freight rates fell ~51% YoY through 2025 and are forecast to fall further in 2026 amid overcapacity and Red Sea route normalisation; US tariffs (~18% average) are dampening trans-Pacific volumes into 2026; domestic trucking/road rates in the US have started to firm modestly after 2024-25 capacity exits.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - Air & Ocean forwarding margins in particular are highly cyclical and levered to global freight rate swings and trade volumes; Domestic Transport and Warehousing are comparatively more stable/annuity-like but still GDP/trade sensitive
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-moderate direct P&L sensitivity (floating-rate debt, no swaps currently in place) but meaningful indirect sensitivity via cost of capex funding and lease finance costs, and via risk-appetite for the group's premium equity multiple
key_input_costs: Diesel/fuel (largely pass-through via fuel adjustment factors)
Wages and labour (largest single cost line, ~22% of revenue)
Air and ocean freight/carrier capacity costs
Land and construction costs for warehousing capex programme

recent_developments.event: FY2026 annual result (year to 31 March 2026): revenue NZ$5,383.5m (+2.8%), PBT $350.9m (-8.5%), NPAT $251.0m (-8.5%); full dividends for the year totalled 172cps; net capex $189m; FY2027 total capex guided at $234m (of which ~$174m property)

Management flagged H1 FY2026 profit weakness (slow to adjust cost structures/freight efficiencies) but noted a materially stronger H2, with momentum continuing into April/May 2026 trading ahead of prior year
Australia's profitability confirmed to exceed New Zealand's for a second consecutive year, a structural milestone for the group
Bryan Mogridge announced retirement from the Board after 23 years' service, effective at the 30 July 2026 Annual Meeting

H1 FY2026 interim result (six months to 30 September 2025): revenue $2,605.7m (+2.1%), PBT $131.7m (down 18.3%), NPAT $93.4m (down 18.5%); interim dividend of 85.0 cents per share maintained flat versus prior year despite the profit decline
US tariff implementation disrupted global supply chains through the year; Mainfreight navigated 'satisfactory' trade-lane conditions overall despite the disruption, per Chairman's commentary

Continued heavy investment in New Zealand and Australian warehousing/cross-dock network (new facilities in Auckland, Whanganui, Hastings, New Plymouth, Brisbane, Melbourne, Townsville) while European land investment was explicitly delayed and US (Chicago) land banked pending improved regional profitability

items.notes: Up from NZ$189m net capex in FY2026; of which ~$174m is property/land & buildings (further ~$102m of property capex flagged for FY2028)

Management stated trading through April and May 2026 improved on the year prior, with strong sales growth continuing across all regions; no explicit revenue/PBT numeric guidance given (Mainfreight does not issue formal earnings guidance)

items.target: Final dividend 87.0 cents per share (fully imputed) plus 15.35 cents supplementary
items.notes: Flat versus the FY2025 final/FY2026 interim dividends despite the PBT/NPAT decline, signalling management confidence in the earnings trajectory

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Bruce Plested and GMD Don Braid both characterised FY2026 as a disappointing year on profitability (H1 profit down 18% on slow cost/efficiency adjustment) but highlighted a materially stronger H2 and continuing improvement into early FY2027. Management reiterated that Europe and Americas warehousing/cross-dock investment will only resume 'when profitability reaches acceptable levels', while NZ and Australia continue to receive the bulk of new capital given superior returns. No formal numeric FY2027 revenue/profit guidance is provided (consistent with historical practice); the company instead publishes a rolling five/six-year strategic roadmap with qualitative/operational milestones (e.g., an aspirational $10bn Group revenue by FY2029/30).

bull_case: Founder-led, owner-operator culture with genuine long-tenured management depth (regional leaders with 15-31 years' tenure) is a hard-to-replicate structural advantage versus centrally managed global peers
Dominant and still-growing market share in NZ/Australia (Australia's profit now exceeds NZ's) provides a highly cash-generative core funding continued international expansion

Optionality in Europe, Americas and Asia represents a multi-year runway for margin expansion as these currently sub-scale or loss-making networks mature - management sees the Americas in particular as its greatest untapped opportunity

Owned property base (~$1.53bn) and disciplined balance sheet (48.6% equity/assets, low net bank debt) provide resilience through freight cycles and optionality to accelerate capex when returns improve

History of trading at a premium multiple reflects a market view this is a rare, high-quality compounder; a freight-rate cycle recovery (after the FY2026 trough) could drive a strong earnings rebound given operating leverage
bear_case: FY2026 showed the model's vulnerability to a freight-rate/cost-inflation squeeze: PBT fell 8.5% (10.7% in constant currency) even as revenue grew, exposing weak internal cost discipline that took two halves to correct

Europe and Americas have now underperformed for well over a decade of investment with no clear profitability inflection date; capital continues to be committed (or land-banked) in regions generating negative or marginal returns
Heavy, ongoing capex requirement (NZ$234m guided FY2027, rising land/construction costs) structurally caps free cash flow conversion versus asset-light global forwarding peers

Premium NZX valuation multiple leaves little room for earnings disappointment; a prolonged global freight-rate downturn (ocean rates forecast to fall further into 2026 on overcapacity) could compress Air & Ocean margins further and trigger material de-rating

Key-person/succession risk around an 83-year-old founder-Chairman with no announced succession plan, and FX translation exposure (66% of revenue offshore) create earnings volatility largely outside management's control
